title: Domain-tiered hierarchical sampling for quantization calibration bundles
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: produce reproducible, per-domain calibration bundles tailored for FP8 and INT8 quantization validation that reflect production traffic distribution while prioritizing high-impact edge cases. The deliverable is an automated pipeline that outputs domain-tiered calibration bundles (N examples/domain) with metadata required by the quantization harness (tokenized lengths, prefix hashes, failure signals, and sampling provenance).

Background: Existing calibration packs tend to either oversample frequent templates or rely on uniform reservoir strategies that miss rare but high-error patterns. For recent FP8/INT8 kernels we observed failure modes concentrated in long-context chains, short ambiguous prompts, and prompts with rare tokens (emoji, code snippets). We need a sampling strategy that preserves production representativeness for unit-cost validation while increasing recall for likely quantization regressions.

Scope: engineering-side pipeline (data extraction, stratified sampling, anchor exemplar seeding, export to S3), integration with calibration harness (quant-eval), and basic dashboarding to track per-domain calibration coverage and quant-error proxies. Not in scope: model retraining, prompt rewriting, or customer-facing UI changes.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A reproducible job (Dag run) that emits one calibration bundle per active domain with deterministic seed and metadata.
2) Bundles include: original prompt, tokenized length, prefix hash, user-cohort tag, recency score, rarity score, failure-signal flags, and sampling weight.
3) Default bundle sizes: small domains=1k, medium=5k, large=20k (configurable).
4) Demonstrated improved detection of quantization regressions: run on 3 historical rollouts and show >=15% relative increase in per-domain pathologies flagged vs baseline reservoir sampling.
5) Integration test: quant-eval pipeline accepts the bundles and completes end-to-end for FP8 and INT8 profiles.
6) Documentation: Confluence how-to and a short runbook for rerun/augmentation.
7) Dashboard: per-domain coverage and token-length distribution visible in Perfboard (links in comments).
tasks:
- Design sampling algorithm and define stratification axes (domain, token-length bucket, recency bins, rarity quartiles, failure-signal).
- Implement extractor: stable export from production logging (controlled sampling window + privacy filters).
- Implement hierarchical sampler: tiered quotas with importance reweighting and recency decay.
- Anchor seeding: add curated exemplars per domain (security/legal/PII safe) to ensure coverage of known edge cases.
- Export schema: JSONL with required fields and provenance.
- Add unit tests and determinism checks.
- Run offline experiments comparing against existing reservoir and stratified baselines.
- Create Confluence doc and alerting for drift in calibration distribution.
design_decisions:
- Use hierarchical quotas to guarantee minimum per-domain representation while allowing head domains to scale with log(volume).
- Importance signal is a composite score: 0.5 * failure_signal + 0.2 * rarity_score + 0.2 * recency_score + 0.1 * length_penalty. We will tune weights empirically.
- Recency implemented as exponential decay (half-life 30 days) rather than sliding window to preserve long-tail examples.
- Anchor exemplars stored in a separate vault and merged at sampling time to avoid accidental exposure. Anchors count toward domain quota but are tagged.
- Default token-length buckets: [0-32,33-128,129-512,513+]. This reduces leakage between short single-token prompts and long-context generations where quant errors concentrate.
- Determinism via explicit RNG seed derived from job_id + domain hashed with HMAC_SHA256.
experiments_and_metrics:
Planned experiments: A) Compare detection rate of quantization outliers (logit-diff and perplexity spike) across 3 sampling strategies: reservoir (baseline), naive stratified, hierarchical-importance sampler. B) Ablations on importance weights and recency half-life.
Metrics: per-domain recall@k for flagged regression examples, false positive rate on synthetic no-change traffic, mean token-length drift vs production, runtime cost of quant-eval per bundle, and proportion of rare-token examples included. Success threshold: hierarchical sampler should increase recall@k by >=15% without >5% increase in false positives and keep eval compute cost within 10%.
implementation_notes:
- Data source: event logs S3 path s3://redwood-prod/logs/llm-requests/yyyy-mm-dd/ with redacted_user_id.
- Export intermediate artifacts to s3://redwood-dev/quant-cal-bundles/{cycle}/{domain}/bundle.jsonl.
- Reuse existing tokenization code in infra/tokenizer-service to ensure identical byte-level tokens used by quant-eval.
- Pipeline in airflow: dag quant_calibration_sampler dag_id quant_cal_sampler_v2 schedule weekly with manual triggers for canary runs.
- Use job-level config to set bundle_size per domain mapping file (CSV) stored in configrepo.
- Add a lightweight sample verifier that ensures no PII tokens (regex filters) and that each example has required metadata.
- Provide a small adaptor script to convert bundle -> quant-eval input format (PR link in comments).
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Overfitting sampler to historical failures causing false alarms on new quant kernels. Mitigation: Hold out most recent 7 days for validation and run ablation on unseen kernels.
Risk: Privacy leakage when anchors are merged. Mitigation: Strict review of anchor list and KMS-protected vault + access controls.
Risk: Pipeline nondeterminism due to log replay ordering. Mitigation: deterministic seed + ordered sorting by event_ts then request_id.
